To address these challenges and facilitate real-time IE on mobile, we introduce an extremely lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework with around 4K parameters. Conclusion In this paper, we introduce MobileIE, a lightweight CNN with only 4K parameters designed for real-time image enhancement on mobile devices. MobileIE combines simplicity with high performance across low-light image enhancement, underwater image enhancement, and image signal processing tasks. Key components such as the MBRConv, Feature Self-Transform module, Hierarchical Dual-Path Attention mechanism, and Local Variance-Weighted loss enable MobileIE to achieve superior results while maintaining an inference time of around 0.9 ms. Furthermore, MobileIE can be easily deployed on any commercial mobile device with minimal computational overhead and efficient resource utilization. However, deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained platforms, such as mobile devices, remains challenging due to high computation and memory demands. To address these challenges and facilitate real-time IE on mobile, we introduce an extremely lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework with around 4K parameters. Our approach integrates reparameterization with an Incremental Weight Optimization strategy to ensure efficiency. Additionally, we enhance performance with a Feature Self-Transposition module and a Hierarchical Dual-Path Attention mechanism, optimized with a Local Variance-Weighted loss. However, their reliance on computationally expensive self-attention mechanisms and iterative diffusion processes makes them unsuitable for mobile devices. While lightweight models have been developed to reduce computational complexity using parameter compression and low-FLOPs architecture designs [57, 59, 63, 80, 83], these approaches often compromise enhancement quality, making it challenging to achieve high performance across a wide range of degradation scenarios [1]. Furthermore, the increasing demand for high-resolution images [69] exacerbates the computational burdens on mobile platforms. Besides facing computational bottlenecks, current IE methods are typically optimized for specific degradation types, restricting their adaptability. Although advanced operators [10, 11] have shown effectiveness in certain tasks, their complexity makes them unsuitable for mobile deployment. Consequently, designing a universal and efficient network capable of real-time IE on resource-constrained devices remains a significant research challenge. We believe that mobile-based IE should strike a balance between speed and performance, leveraging general architectures and hardware-friendly operators [66, 88]. To address these challenges, we introduce MobileIE, an efficient method designed for real-time enhancement in resource-constrained environments, optimizing both performance and resource utilization. Figure 7. General method proposed by AVC2 team Team AVC2 introduced MobileIE, a lightweight image enhancement network designed for mobile deployment that balances performance and efficiency using reparameterization as illustrated in Fig. 7. The architecture begins with an MBRConv \(5 \times 5\) layer followed by a PReLU activation. The subsequent main body consists of two sequential blocks; each block contains an MBRConv \(3 \times 3\) layer followed by a Feature Self-Transform (FST) module, incorporating residual connections and bias vectors for feature refinement. After these blocks, a Hierarchical Dual-Path Attention (HDPA) module is employed to refine features. Upsampling is achieved through a Pixel Shuffle layer, followed by a final MBRConv \(3 \times 3\) layer generating the output image. A key aspect is the MBRConv block, which utilizes multiple parallel convolutional branches with batch normalization during training; these are reparameterized into standard single convolutional layers for efficient inference. The MobileIE model was trained using \(L_1\) loss, chosen for its tendency to encourage sharper image reconstruction compared to \(L_2\). The Adam optimizer was used with a cosine annealing learning rate schedule, initialized at 0.001 after a 10-epoch warm-up phase at a fixed rate of \(1 \mathrm{e}{-6}\). The learning rate was reset every 50 epochs before gradually decaying. Training was performed for a total of 5,000 epochs with a batch size of 32. For training data, the team exclusively used the Sony subset provided by the challenge, comprising 162,000 paired images for training and 2,500 for validation. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- MobileIE: An Extremely Lightweight and Effective ConvNet for Real-Time Image Enhancement on Mobile Devices (https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2025/supplemental/Yan_MobileIE_An_Extremely_ICCV_2025_supplemental.pdf) 【turn285687search30】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last year; This paper introduces MobileIE, a lightweight CNN for image enhancement.
